about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Marinated Artichoke Hearts
recipes.summary: Tender artichoke quarters tossed in lemon, garlic, oregano and olive oil, ready for a snack plate.

items: 400g can artichoke hearts, drained and quartered

steps: Pat the artichokes dry on paper towel so the marinade clings.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, chilli and salt until combined.
Toss the artichokes through the marinade until evenly coated, then spoon into a jar or bowl and serve with toothpicks.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 4 quarters. Plus 30 minutes marinating at room temperature, or up to 5 days in the fridge; bring to room temperature before serving.

recipes.title: Garlic and Thyme Marinated Mushrooms
recipes.summary: Tapas-style button mushrooms softened in a sherry vinegar and thyme marinade.
steps: Warm 1 tbsp of the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes, until golden and no liquid remains.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Tip into a bowl and stir through the remaining oil, vinegar, salt and pepper until glossy.
Serve warm or at room temperature with toothpicks.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/2 cup. Plus 1 hour marinating. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Pickled Beetroot Eggs
recipes.summary: Hard-boiled eggs steeped in a sweet-sharp beetroot brine until pink, a pub-style snack.
steps: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Cool in iced water and peel.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and peppercorns for 3 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then cool.
Pack the eggs and beetroot into a clean jar and pour over the brine until covered.
Seal and keep in the fridge until the eggs are pink through the outer white.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 egg with a few beetroot slices. Plus 2 days pickling.
Food safety: use only clean, sterilised jars, keep the jar in the fridge at all times, and eat within 5 days.

recipes.title: Quick Pickled Jalapenos
recipes.summary: Crisp pickled jalapeno rings with garlic and cumin for nachos and sliders.
steps: Pack the jalapeno rings and garlic into a clean jar.
Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and cumin until the sugar and salt dissolve, then pour over the jalapenos until covered.
Cool, then seal and refrigerate.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 25g (a small handful). Plus 1 day pickling. Keeps 3 weeks in the fridge. Wear gloves when slicing.

recipes.title: Korean Style Spicy Cucumber Pickle
recipes.summary: Salted cucumber chunks tossed in chilli flakes, garlic, sesame and a little sugar, ready in an hour.
steps: Toss the cucumber with the salt and leave in a colander until it releases water, then squeeze lightly and dry.
Mix the chilli flakes, garlic, soy sauce, vinegar and sugar into a paste.
Toss the cucumber, paste, spring onion and sesame seeds together until evenly coated.
Serve as a crunchy side snack.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1 cup. Plus 20 minutes salting. Best within 2 days.

recipes.title: Giardiniera Italian Pickled Vegetables
recipes.summary: Crunchy carrot, cauliflower, celery and capsicum in a tangy herbed brine.
steps: Pack all the vegetables into a clean jar.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, oregano and garlic for 3 minutes until the sugar and salt dissolve, then pour over the vegetables until just covered.
Cool, then seal and refrigerate.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/2 cup. Plus 1 day pickling. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

recipes.title: Marinated Feta Cubes
recipes.summary: Salty feta cubes in olive oil with lemon peel, thyme and chilli to spear or spread.
steps: Pack the feta into a clean jar.
Mix the oil, lemon zest, thyme, chilli and peppercorns and pour over the feta until fully covered.
Seal and refrigerate until the flavours develop, then serve with toothpicks.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian (check the feta label for non-animal rennet). Per serving: about 5 cubes with some oil. Plus 4 hours marinating. Keeps 1 week in the fridge.

recipes.title: Tamari Roasted Chickpeas
recipes.summary: Crunchy chickpeas roasted with tamari and smoked paprika for a high-fibre desk snack.

items: 2 x 400g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Dry the chickpeas very well on a clean tea towel.
Toss with the oil, tamari, paprika and garlic powder.
Roast on a lined tray for 30 minutes, shaking twice, until crisp and deep golden.
Cool on the tray, where they crisp further.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/2 cup. Store in an open container; sealed jars soften them. Best within 3 days.

recipes.title: Vegan Sun-Dried Tomato and White Bean Spread
recipes.summary: A cheese-free spread of cannellini beans, sun-dried tomatoes and basil on toasted sourdough.

items: 400g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Blend the beans, sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, oil, lemon juice, basil and salt until thick and nearly smooth.
Toast the sourdough until golden and cut each slice in half.
Spread the toast generously with the bean mixture until covered, then serve.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 half slice with spread. The spread alone keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Vegan Mushroom and Walnut Pate
recipes.summary: A rich, cheese-free pate of mushrooms, walnuts and white beans on toasted sourdough.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil for 4 minutes until soft, add the mushrooms, garlic and thyme and cook for 8 minutes until all the liquid has gone.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Blend the mushroom mixture, walnuts, beans and soy sauce until thick and spreadable.
Toast the sourdough until golden, cut each slice in half and serve with the pate.
notes: Snack. Vegan (check the bread label). Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 1 half slice with pate. Plus 2 hours chilling. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Vegan Potato and Carrot Nacho Dip
recipes.summary: A cheese-free orange dip made from potato, carrot and tahini, with a smoky kick, served with corn chips.
steps: Simmer the potato, carrot, onion and garlic in water for 18 minutes, until very soft, then reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking water and drain.
Blend the vegetables with the tahini, oil, lemon juice, paprika and salt, adding the reserved water until smooth and pourable.
Serve warm with the corn chips.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/3 cup dip with 16g of chips. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; thin with water when reheating.

recipes.title: Seed Cracker Dippers
recipes.summary: Crisp olive oil crackers packed with sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds, sturdy enough for any dip.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Mix the flour, seeds and salt, then stir in the oil and water to a firm dough.
Roll the dough very thinly between two sheets of baking paper and cut into 32 small rectangles.
Bake on a lined tray for 22 minutes, turning the tray halfway, until golden and crisp.
Cool on a wire rack, where they crisp further.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 crackers. Contains gluten and sesame. Keeps 7 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Vegan Stuffed Mini Capsicums
recipes.summary: Sweet mini capsicum halves filled with a lemony basil tofu cream, baked until the edges soften.

items: 8 mini capsicums, halved lengthways and deseeded

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Roast the capsicum halves cut side up on a lined tray for 8 minutes until just soft.
Blend the tofu, oil, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt until creamy, then stir in the basil.
Spoon the filling into the capsicums and bake for 4 minutes more until warmed through.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Snack. Vegan, cheese-free. Per serving: 4 halves. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Sunflower Seed Chocolate Oat Balls
recipes.summary: Nut-free, school-safe oat balls rolled in coconut, sweetened with honey.
steps: Mix the oats, ground sunflower seeds, honey, chocolate chips and water until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Roll into 12 balls and coat each in the coconut.
Place on a tray and keep cold until firm.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free and school-safe (check the chocolate label for traces). Per serving: 2 balls. Plus 30 minutes chilling. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Nut-Free Oat and Seed Bars
recipes.summary: Chewy baked bars with oats, sultanas and seeds, free of nuts for lunchboxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Warm the honey and oil together until runny, then mix with the oats, seeds, sultanas, cinnamon and egg.
Press firmly into the tin and bake for 25 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free and school-safe (check labels for traces). Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: the egg is fully cooked through in the bake; keep the bars refrigerated if your kitchen is warm.

recipes.title: Nut-Free Veggie Pizza Scrolls
recipes.summary: Soft yoghurt-dough scrolls with tomato paste, mozzarella and capsicum for lunchboxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional). Mix the flour and yoghurt to a soft dough and knead briefly until smooth.
Roll into a 25 x 35cm rectangle, spread with the tomato paste and scatter with the mozzarella, capsicum and oregano.
Roll up from the long side, cut into 12 slices and place cut side up on a lined tray.
Bake for 20 minutes, until puffed and golden.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free and school-safe. Per serving: 2 scrolls. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Nut-Free Apple Oat Muffins
recipes.summary: Moist wholemeal muffins with grated apple, oats and cinnamon.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the oats, flour, baking powder, sugar and cinnamon, then stir in the apple, egg, milk and oil until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a wire rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free and school-safe. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Chocolate Oat Breakfast Bars
recipes.summary: Soft baked oat bars with cocoa and chocolate chips for breakfast on the go.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, cocoa and baking powder, then stir in the honey, milk, eggs and oil, followed by half the chocolate chips.
Spread into the tin, scatter with the remaining chips and bake for 25 minutes, until firm in the centre.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container; freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Mixed Berry Oat Breakfast Bars
recipes.summary: Yoghurt and honey oat bars studded with frozen berries.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, baking powder and cinnamon, then stir in the yoghurt, eggs, honey and oil until combined, and fold in the frozen berries.
Spread into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until golden and set in the centre.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Tropical Coconut Oat Breakfast Bars
recipes.summary: Chewy oat bars with coconut, pineapple and honey for a quick breakfast.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, coconut, baking powder and salt, then stir in the pineapple, eggs, honey and coconut oil until combined.
Press into the tin and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and firm.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container; freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Oat Breakfast Squares
recipes.summary: Spiced oat squares with mashed pumpkin and sultanas, soft and not too sweet.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, baking powder and spices, then stir in the pumpkin, eggs, honey and oil, and fold in the sultanas.
Spread into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until set and golden at the edges.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze for up to 2 months.
